clue.text: New medical method that has a point, figuratively speaking

definitions.text: that has a point, figuratively speaking

indicators.note: new here means the word medical is made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a method is a system, an organised way of doing things

explanation.surface: A novel medical technique that, metaphorically, has a point to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges MEDICAL into DECIMAL. 'Figuratively' is the joke: the point in question is the one among figures, as in 3.5.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting in tens uses a dot to separate whole numbers from fractions, so the scheme literally has a point among its figures.

clue.text: Sending down from Oriel

parts.note: reads like expelling a student from Oriel College, Oxford, but an oriel is also a bay window, and this is throwing someone out of a window

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sending down' is the Oxbridge term for expelling a student, and Oriel is an Oxford college; the second sense is a projecting upper window.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means throwing a person or thing out of a window, here an oriel window.

clue.text: Empty vault

explanation.definitionFit: To empty a room is to clear it, and to vault a fence or bar is to clear it by jumping over.

clue.text: Easy for one to change his mind about new map

indicators.note: about means the first jumbled group goes around the second
to change asks for the letters of his mind to be put in another order
new tells us the word map is laid out afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone is said to change their mind over a new map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy' looks like an adjective but is a name: Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Captain Marryat's naval novel. Two separate anagrams, one wrapped round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Easy, of Marryat's novel Mr Midshipman Easy, holds a junior naval officer's rank, so he is an example.

clue.text: Bloodthirsty creature seen to strike victim

parts.note: to lam is an old informal word for to beat or hit
prey is a victim, something hunted

explanation.surface: A vicious animal is spotted attacking its quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: This jawless eel-like fish fastens onto other fish and sucks their blood.

clue.text: Without hesitation, take lots of time in New York city

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: yonks is British slang for a very long time
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Advice to spend a long time in a city in New York without dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but here has its old sense, outside. Yonks is British slang for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a city in Westchester County, just north of the Bronx in New York State.

clue.text: Food course

explanation.definitionFit: Tack is food, as in hard tack, a sailor's ship's biscuit; a course is a sailing tack, a line steered against the wind.

clue.text: City — later than 1 1 PM

parts.note: an Australian city whose clocks run ahead of Britain's, so its time is later than ours, and which shares its name with a Victorian prime minister

explanation.walkthrough: PM reads as 'evening' but also as Prime Minister: Lord Melbourne was Queen Victoria's first premier, and the Australian city is many hours ahead of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian state capital is named after Lord Melbourne, British prime minister in the 1830s.

clue.text: Game requiring action replays

parts.note: sounds like television sport, but is a children's game in which everyone copies whatever the person in front does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Action replays' suggests television sport; here the replaying is the players repeating each action of the one at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: In this children's pastime every player must imitate the moves of the person heading the line.

clue.text: Slip, for example, made by female novelist? Just the opposite!

parts.note: Rachel Field was an American novelist, so a thing of hers is Field's
female, turned by 'Just the opposite!' into its opposite, gives a man

explanation.surface: Asks whether a slip of paper or underwear was made by a woman writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite!' flips 'female' to male: not a female made by a novelist but a man made by Field. Slip is a fielding position in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Slip is a close catching position in cricket, and the player standing there is one of the team's outfield players.

clue.text: Instrument giving nuclear group zero reading

parts.note: a cell is a small core group in an organisation, and also has a nucleus
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A meter showing that a nuclear team's dial reads nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large bowed string instrument of the violin family, played seated.

clue.text: Quarter or half of ten or three

indicators.note: half of means taking the middle five of the ten letters in ten or three

explanation.surface: A puzzle in fractions: a quarter, or half of thirteen-ish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes the central five letters of the ten in TENORTHREE.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four cardinal compass points, so a quarter of the compass.

clue.text: Drum music

explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a drum or spool for winding thread or line, and a lively Scottish or Irish dance tune.

clue.text: Aim for internal prison reform

indicators.note: reform, with internal, means the inner letters of the word for prison are moved about

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail

explanation.surface: A goal of improving conditions inside jails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internal' tells you only the inner pair of GAOL (British for jail) changes places in the 'reform'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim is a target or objective, what one is striving for.

clue.text: One who works actively among constituents of a Grecian MP

indicators.note: constituents of says the letters of a Grecian MP are the ingredients to be rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone busy among the voters of a Greek member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' suggests voters, but signals that the letters of A GRECIAN MP are the parts to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who campaigns works energetically for a cause.

clue.text: Awkward spot — sailor's left to turn round in it

indicators.note: in means the turned piece sits within the other

parts.note: to spot is to spy, to catch sight of

indicators.note: to turn round asks for the word for the sailor's left to be read backwards

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A tricky situation in which a sailor has to turn about inside some place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' here is the British slang sense, bad-tempered; 'spot' is a verb, to catch sight of.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for bad-tempered and difficult, quick to take offence.

clue.text: Parliamentarian's double cape

parts.note: to double a headland is to sail round it, so double means round
a cape is a head, a headland

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament has a two-layer cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Parliamentarian's' stands for 'is'. Roundheads were the Parliament side in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundheads were supporters of Parliament against the King in the English Civil War, named for their cropped hair.

clue.text: A couple of scraps for bird

parts.note: to spar is to have a fight, one scrap
a row is a quarrel, the second scrap

explanation.surface: Two bits of food left over for a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scraps' tempts as leftover food; here they are fights.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown songbird common around houses.

clue.text: Plant a conversation piece on stage

explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is a garden plant with edible stalks; actors in a crowd scene mutter it to sound like background chatter.

clue.text: Sort of attire bishop put on top?

definitions.text: Sort of attire bishop put on top?

indicators.note: put on top means the bishop's letter is placed above the rest in this down clue

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: sort of signals the letters of attire are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a churchman's clothing is the kind a bishop wears on his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges ATTIRE into IRETTA, under B. The whole clue also describes the answer: a garment a churchman puts on his head.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is a square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy, a piece of clerical dress for the head.

clue.text: Quick-tempered and energetic king's entered

indicators.note: entered means the king's letter has gone inside

parts.note: peppy is informal for lively
ER, Edward Rex, stands for a king called Edward; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: Describes a hot-headed, vigorous king making his entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Edward Rex) goes into PEPPY.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppery person is hot-tempered, like the sharp spice.

clue.text: No amateur's first-class century could be unexciting?

parts.note: a professional is no amateur, and the 's adds the S
A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A professional's top-class cricket hundred might be dull.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 ('first-class') is read as AI. 'century' suggests a cricket score of a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means dull and matter-of-fact, lacking imagination like plain prose.

clue.text: Sort of sum made when one cleans up?

definitions.text: Sort of sum made when one cleans up?

parts.words: Sort of sum made when one cleans up?
parts.note: a large amount of money is a nice round one, the kind won when someone cleans up; and cleaning up a room makes it neat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleans up' means both to win a lot of money and to put a room in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A considerable amount of money is called this, and a room that has been cleaned up is also this.

clue.text: Not out on a river here

annotationWithheld.why: 'Not out on a river here' (ARNO): A + R(iver) leaves NO for 'Not out on' and no parse uses every word fairly; no source found to confirm the setter's intent.
annotationWithheld.clue: Not out on a river here

clue.text: Periodical that's without an idea

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the letters for that's surround the other piece

parts.note: i.e., id est, means that is
a mag is a magazine, a periodical

explanation.surface: A magazine that lacks any concept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but has its old sense, outside; 'that's' stands for the Latin abbreviation id est.
explanation.definitionFit: A mental picture or notion of something.

clue.text: Guy's part, perhaps, In presentation

explanation.definitionFit: Guy's is a London hospital, so one of its wards is a section of it; a prize is something presented.

clue.text: Insect audible in Eastern country

indicators.note: audible says the word for the insect is heard, as spoken

parts.note: a louse is a small parasitic insect

explanation.surface: A bug can be heard in an Asian nation.
explanation.walkthrough: In older British speech the country rhymed with 'louse'.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked country in South-East Asia, bordering Vietnam and Thailand.

clue.text: Zero backing for a repertory theatre

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O

indicators.note: backing means the words a repertory are read from right to left

parts.note: rep is short for repertory

explanation.surface: A repertory theatre receives no support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support, but it turns A REP into PERA after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is a dramatic art form, a kind of musical drama staged in a theatre, much as theatre is a kind of performance.

clue.text: Coach players such as those under Gilpin's captaincy

definitions.text: such as those under Gilpin's captaincy

parts.note: to coach is to train
a band is a group of musicians, players

explanation.surface: Coaching a team of players like those led by a captain called Gilpin.
explanation.walkthrough: John Gilpin, in Cowper's comic poem, was 'a trainband captain'; trainbands were London's old citizen militia.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gilpin in William Cowper's ballad captained a company of this London citizen militia.

clue.text: Messenger comes from expedition with proposition

parts.note: expedition in the sense of speed or promptness is dispatch
a rider is a proposition or clause added to a verdict or bill

explanation.surface: A courier arrives from a journey with an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' tempts as a journey; here it means speed. A rider is an added clause.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcyclist or horseman who carries urgent messages, especially military ones.
